title: Strong unitary designs in optimal depth and space
abstract: Unitary designs provide finite-moment approximations to Haar-random unitaries, with wide-ranging applications across physics and quantum information, from scrambling and black-hole dynamics to foundational primitives in quantum algorithms. Strong unitary designs capture a more demanding operational notion of approximation, requiring indistinguishability from Haar randomness even for quantum algorithms that may access a unitary not only in the forward direction, but also through its inverse, transpose, and complex conjugate. Motivated by the physical requirement that scrambling arise within the system itself, Schuster, Ma, Lombardi, Brandão, and Huang (arXiv:2509.26310) left open whether strong unitary designs can be generated in logarithmic depth using only the system qubits. For every fixed design order $k$ and measurable-error tolerance, we construct strong approximate unitary $k$-designs in optimal $Θ(\log n)$ all-to-all circuit depth using only the $n$ original system qubits. Our new ingredient is a logarithmic-depth Pauli-mixing bound for the perfect-matching ensemble, whose layers pair the qubits uniformly at random and apply independent random two-qubit gates. This bound controls the mixed forward-reverse two-query case, which we combine with existing design and gluing results to obtain strong unitary designs of arbitrary fixed order.

bite.hook: Strong unitary designs can be generated in optimal logarithmic circuit depth using zero auxiliary qubits.
tldr: Constructed strong approximate unitary k-designs using optimal Θ(log n) circuit depth without extra workspace qubits.
Derived a logarithmic-depth Pauli-mixing bound for random perfect-matching two-qubit gate layers.
Proved that circuits can scramble quantum information against forward, inverse, and transpose queries using only system qubits.
bite.whyItMatters: Unitary designs are essential benchmarks for quantum algorithms, thermalization, and black hole models; achieving them with minimal circuit depth and no extra qubits makes them practically realizable.
bite.eli5: Think of a magic deck of cards that shuffles itself so thoroughly that even inspecting it backwards or sideways looks completely random. The authors proved a recipe to achieve this perfect shuffle in the shortest possible time without adding extra blank cards.

glossary.shortDef: An ensemble of unitary operators mimicking the statistical moments of uniform Haar-random unitaries.
glossary.eli5Def: A small, practical set of quantum operations that statistically mimics total quantum randomness.

glossary.shortDef: The unique, uniform probability distribution over continuous compact groups like unitary matrices.
glossary.eli5Def: The gold-standard mathematical definition of choosing a quantum transformation completely uniformly at random.

glossary.shortDef: The rapid delocalization and dispersal of local quantum information across an entire many-body system.
glossary.eli5Def: How quantum information gets spread out and hidden across all particles in a system, like ink dissolving in water.
